newsitem.title: INDIA: India police arrest three, seize explosives.
newsitem.headline: India police arrest three, seize explosives.

text.p: Indian police on Tuesday seized a large quantity of sophisticated explosives after they arrested three suspected Kashmiri militants in the Indian capital.
A Delhi police spokesman said a raid on a city hotel unearthed about five kg (11 lb) of the powerful RDX explosive along with detonators, timers, and some incriminating documents.
The police said the three men had planned to use the explosive for bomb attacks ahead of India's Republic Day celebrations on January 26.
"With their arrest a series of possible attacks in the capital before or during the Republic Day celebrations has been averted," the spokesman said.
It was the second seizure of explosives in the capital this month, the police said.
The spokesman said the men were suspected of links to the Jammu and Kashmir Liberation Front, one of dozens of separatist groups in the troubled northern state which demand independence.
Each year, India observes January 26, the day its constitution first came into force, as Republic Day.
Indian authorities, apprehensive of attacks by militant groups, have tightened security ahead of the event.
Police seized 10 kg of RDX as well as electronic detonators and explosives in a raid in south Delhi earlier this month, and arrested two people.
